Commands v2 method lookup

Find the v3 equivalent of a v2 method. The index is sorted by the first method in each entry. If you already know the v3 name, use the v3 method lookup.

On this page
  • A–H
  • I–R
  • S–W

A–H

  • addRequirements — Call this.run(...) inside a mechanism to require that mechanism. Use Command.requiring(...) when listing requirements explicitly. See where the intake requirement comes from.
  • asProxy / ProxyCommand — Let each child require its mechanism only while it runs. Compare a v2 proxy sequence with v3 await.
  • deadline — A deadline child determines when the group finishes. The group needs the mechanisms required by all its children. Keep drive stopped during a pause.
  • defer / DeferredCommand — Call the factory inside the coroutine body to build the child from the robot’s state at that point. Build a command from the current pose.
  • deferredProxy — Build the child when you reach the stage and let it acquire its own requirement. Combine deferred construction and child requirements.
  • either / select — Use an if or switch inside a coroutine to make a choice while the command runs. See a retry loop and route decision.
  • end / finallyDo — Use whenExited for cleanup whenever the command ends and whenCanceled for cancellation-only work. Follow an intake command through cancellation.

I–R

  • initialize / execute / isFinished — Put setup at the start of the body, repeating work in a loop that pauses each cycle, and completion at the return. Follow an intake command from start to finish.
  • parallel — Use Command.parallel(...) or awaitAll(...) to wait for all children to finish. See two actions run together · WPILib parallel examples ↗ (opens in a new tab).
  • periodic — Call required sensor updates from the robot loop. See where to move periodic updates.
  • race — Use Command.race(...) or awaitAny(...) to continue after the first child finishes and cancel the remaining children. Race a sensor against a timer · WPILib race examples ↗ (opens in a new tab).
  • run / runOnce / runEnd — Use runRepeatedly for work every cycle or a run body that returns immediately for a one-time action. Use whenExited to stop an output when needed. See a repeating drive stop.

S–W

  • sequence — Use a native sequence for a fixed order that keeps its combined requirements. A coordinating coroutine can await each child and let that child control its own mechanisms. Decide when to use a group or a coroutine.
  • setDefaultCommand — Decide where the default should be active and what priority it should have. See joystick drive and alignment · WPILib section on default commands ↗ (opens in a new tab).
  • startEnd — Start the action, pause the command as needed, and use whenExited to stop the action when the command ends. Compare the two intake classes.
  • until / waitUntil / waitSeconds / withTimeout — Decide which condition or duration ends the work and what happens when time runs out. Collect with a time limit.
  • whileTrue — Check press, completion while held, and release. A retry binding can restart the command while the button stays held. Run a roller while a button is held.
  • withInterruptBehavior — Use command priorities to decide which action can take over. See priority and default behavior.
  • withName — Finish a v3 builder with .named(...). See the difference between a builder and a command.
